- [USER] User requested more information about the history of the Alhambra.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Alhambra was constructed during the Moorish reign in the 13th and 14th centuries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The name "Alhambra" comes from the Arabic "Al-Hamra," meaning "the red one," due to the reddish hue of its walls and towers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Alhambra was built as a fortress and royal palace by the Nasrid dynasty and served as the center of political and cultural activity during that period.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] After the Christian conquest of Granada in 1492, the Alhambra was used as a royal palace by the Catholic monarchs, with several additions made to the complex.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Alhambra fell into disrepair over the centuries but was restored in the 19th and 20th centuries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Today, the Alhambra is one of Spain's most visited landmarks and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
